preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.

Abort rather than infer success when persistence, authority or delivery observations are unavailable.

steps.action: Submit one synthetic message with a stable operation key; interrupt its response after persistence.
assertions: The client shows an uncertain outcome rather than claiming failure or durable acceptance without a receipt.
The fixture records the actual commit boundary; do not infer it from HTTP timing.

steps.action: Restart the adapter, query the operation receipt, and replay the same semantic request using the same key.
assertions: Exactly one durable capture exists for that scoped request; the original receipt identifies it.
No proposal was approved, no board mutation occurred, and no new operation key was silently minted.

steps.action: Reuse the operation key with a different semantic payload.
assertions: The service rejects the conflict without changing the first record or leaking it to another principal.

journeys.goal: A changed proposal or revoked scope cannot be executed using stale approval context.

preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.
Use only synthetic records and explicit local credentials. Record exact candidate, configuration, initial persistence counts and operation identifiers.

steps.action: Read a proposal and record its exact revision, target, operation set and actor.
assertions: The inspection is not itself an approval or authority grant.

steps.action: Keep actor scope valid, change the target revision, and attempt execution using the previously reviewed revision.
assertions: The stale-revision control alone rejects execution with zero mutation effects; authorization is still valid.
The adapter reloads for review rather than silently replacing the expected revision.

steps.action: Read the current target revision, revoke actor scope without changing that revision, and attempt execution.
assertions: The permission control alone rejects execution with zero mutation effects; the revision is current.
The adapter does not retry using human credentials, a different principal or an unreviewed replacement proposal.

steps.action: Restore only the fixture-required scope, reload, and inspect the newly authorized current proposal.
assertions: Review is bound to the new proposal tuple; the previous approval is not reused.

journeys.goal: Attempt progress and worker exit cannot fabricate completed human work.
journeys.fixture_ref: authoring-only: isolated workspace handoff simulator (not implemented)
preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.
Use only synthetic records and explicit local credentials. Record exact candidate, configuration, initial persistence counts and operation identifiers.
Abort rather than infer success when persistence, authority or delivery observations are unavailable.

steps.action: Authorize one bounded synthetic investigation, lose the admission acknowledgement, then reconcile.
assertions: One intent links to one admitted attempt; each transport retry does not create a new job.

steps.action: Record progress at sequence 2, replay that identical report, then deliver the earlier sequence 1 report using valid current scope.
assertions: The identical report recovers the current attempt state without a second result or admission.
The older report is identified as stale; it cannot regress the authoritative progress sequence or state.
Observed report receipts and stored state remain separate from these authored expectations; human work remains incomplete.

steps.action: Request cancellation, deliver a late progress event and then a successful worker exit with incomplete acceptance evidence.
assertions: Cancellation requested is distinct from stopped effects; late progress does not overwrite newer authoritative state.
The human commitment remains incomplete; incomplete evidence and the late result remain inspectable.

steps.action: Supply valid acceptance evidence through the fixture and perform the separately authorized human-work transition.
assertions: The completion receipt identifies actor, current revision, actual effects and supporting evidence.
The earlier failed, cancelled or uncertain states remain in history rather than being rewritten as uninterrupted success.

journeys.goal: Missing from an incomplete read is not evidence of deletion, delivery or revoked authority.

preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.
Use only synthetic records and explicit local credentials. Record exact candidate, configuration, initial persistence counts and operation identifiers.
Abort rather than infer success when persistence, authority or delivery observations are unavailable.

steps.action: Read a complete authorized synthetic collection and persist its exact coverage and source identity.
assertions: The fixture records which collection was complete; successful HTTP alone does not establish completeness.

steps.action: Return a capped or partial collection that omits a previously observed item.
assertions: The projection reports limited coverage and preserves the last complete observation without inferring removal.
No outcome receipt, notification claim, destructive action or authority change is created from the omission.

steps.action: Make the source unreachable so no read completes, without truncating or denying anything.
assertions: The state is unknown, never PASS and never an empty collection; it is distinct from partial and from denied.
No outcome receipt, deletion, delivery claim or authority change is created from the failure.

steps.action: Restart the consumer and resume with a complete current collection and authoritative outcome receipts.
assertions: The last complete checkpoint survives; recovery compares only complete observations of the same scoped source.
Delivery and cancellation remain distinct producer outcomes; absence alone cannot decide between them.

steps.action: Independently deny current access without truncating the collection, then release an older authorized response.
assertions: Denied access hides private cached content rather than treating the failure as ordinary stale availability.
Denied is a distinct state from unavailable and from partial; it is not reported as either.
The older response cannot repopulate the cache or visible private projection after the newer denial.

journeys.goal: Cancellation, lease retirement and time expiry are rechecked at the actual admission boundary.

steps.action: Reserve one synthetic attempt, block its final authority read, persist cancellation, then release the still-valid authority response.
assertions: Cancellation observed before the documented launch-admission boundary prevents all launcher invocations.
The unstarted reservation is released without claiming process acknowledgement or reconciled effects.

steps.action: In an independent uncancelled attempt, retire its lease while its final authority read is blocked; release that response.
assertions: The retired owner cannot enter the launcher or alter a newer reservation.
The original attempt identity and retirement evidence remain inspectable.

steps.action: Keep revisions and scope valid while the final authority read consumes the remaining disclosure-grant lifetime.
assertions: The execution clock is sampled after the read; an expired grant prevents disclosure and launch.
A fresh authorized control is separate from the expiry control; no implicit grant extension occurs.

steps.action: Admit another authorized attempt through the documented boundary, then request cancellation before its delayed launch acknowledgement.
assertions: The receipt describes in-flight cancellation, not a guaranteed zero-launch result.
Process acknowledgement and effect reconciliation require separate receiver observations; missing evidence remains unknown.

journeys.goal: Each evidence rung is claimed only for the exact candidate it observed; no rung implies a higher one.
journeys.fixture_ref: authoring-only: isolated workspace handoff simulator (not implemented)
preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.
Use only synthetic records and explicit local credentials. Record exact candidate, configuration, initial persistence counts and operation identifiers.
Abort rather than infer success when persistence, authority or delivery observations are unavailable.

steps.action: Declare a source and a unit rung receipt for one fictional candidate: subject revision, exact source revision, fixture revision or hash, UTC time, environment, proof kind, command and cwd, pass/fail/skip counts, unavailable observations and advisory or operational authority.
assertions: Every named field is present or explicitly recorded as unavailable; an omitted field is not a pass.
A unit rung does not imply an integrated, runtime, installed, device or owner-accepted rung.

steps.action: Declare an integrated rung and a native runtime rung as separate receipts, each with its own command, cwd, environment and counts.
assertions: A skipped or unavailable observation stays unknown and is never counted as a pass.
The runtime receipt names the runtime that actually ran, not the one the integrated rung assumed.

steps.action: Declare an installed rung that records the installed artifact identity as a field distinct from the source revision.
assertions: A source-revision match alone never stands in for the identity of the installed artifact.

steps.action: Declare a device rung that records the device and platform identity beside the installed artifact identity.
assertions: A rung observed on one device or platform makes no claim about another.

steps.action: Declare the owner-accepted rung as a slot that only an owner-supplied record can fill.
assertions: No agent, model or lower rung can fill or infer the owner record; absent means open.
Every rung stays advisory and not run in this pack; no execution claim is made.

steps.action: Change the candidate revision after the higher rungs were declared, then re-read every rung.
assertions: No rung transfers to the new candidate revision; each must be re-observed against it.
The earlier receipts stay inspectable as history for the earlier revision.

journeys.goal: A consumer catches up through outcome lookup for known IDs plus a commit-ordered feed for unseen ones, without skipping or splitting.
journeys.fixture_ref: authoring-only: isolated workspace handoff simulator (not implemented)
preconditions: This is authoring-only data. Implement and approve an isolated fixture before attempting execution; the synthetic revision is not a real checkout.
Use only synthetic records and explicit local credentials. Record exact candidate, configuration, initial persistence counts and operation identifiers.
Abort rather than infer success when persistence, authority or delivery observations are unavailable.

steps.action: Look up the outcome of every already-known ID directly, independent of the feed.
assertions: A known ID missing from the feed is resolved by lookup, never by inference from absence.

steps.action: Start a consumer with no saved position and apply the first-run floor.
assertions: The floor bounds the first read in commit order; items before it are reported as not examined, not as absent.

steps.action: Run two passes where each pass re-reads an inclusive overlap with the previous pass and continues exclusively beyond it.
assertions: The inclusive overlap re-delivers boundary items so an item committed late is not lost.
Continuation past the overlap is exclusive; no item is processed twice as new.

steps.action: Serve a page boundary that falls inside a group of items sharing one timestamp.
assertions: A page never splits one timestamp group; the whole group moves to one page.
A resume position never lands inside a group.

steps.action: Defer an item, advance the resume position past it, then resume.
assertions: A deferred item is never skipped by a resume position; it remains pending until resolved.
A failed read does not advance the position.

steps.action: Apply one fix round for a reviewed finding in a fictional expiry, cursor and resume-position component.
assertions: The round records which findings it addresses and which seam it changed.

steps.action: Run one verification scoped to the fix diff, covering the changed seam and its neighbours.
assertions: Expiry does not drop rows that are still recoverable.
A cursor does not advance on a failed read.
A resume position does not skip deferred rows.
These three are examples of defects past fix rounds introduced; the list is illustrative, not complete.

steps.action: Record the verification as a receipt tied to the exact fix revision and report skipped checks.
assertions: A verification of an earlier revision does not cover the fix; an unrun check is reported as not run.
